key_value_text.quote: a_mu = 116,592,0705(148) x 10^-12 (127 ppb) when combined with our previous results. The new experimental world average, dominated by the measurements at FNAL, is a_mu(exp) =116,592,0715(145) x 10^-12 (124 ppb).

name: Measurement of the Positive Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment to 127 ppb

significance.locator: arXiv:2506.03069 abstract / Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 101802 (2025); no single sigma-significance-vs-Standard-Model figure stated in the abstract text fetched
significance.note: Final combined-experiment precision result; no single sigma-significance-vs-Standard-Model figure was fetched in this session (Standard Model prediction itself has an unresolved lattice-vs-data-driven tension noted elsewhere in the literature, not asserted here).

summary.plain: Fermilab's final, most precise measurement of the muon's magnetic wobble, using all six runs of data and more than doubling the precision of the world average.
summary.technical: Final Muon g-2 (E989) result combining all six data-taking runs (2018-2023) for a_mu = 116,592,0705(148)x10^-12 (127 ppb), improving the world average precision by over a factor of four relative to pre-Fermilab measurements.

title: Measurement of the Positive Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment to 127 ppb
why_it_matters: This is the collaboration's final planned measurement of a_mu, closing out the experimental side of the g-2 anomaly question pending continued refinement of the Standard Model theoretical prediction.
